name: silu_exp2_recip
notes: One XMEM row (128 elements) per iteration, 11 instruction words per row (9 of them multiplies), all hardware instructions, in e4, e5, dynamic and fp32. exp2 of a positive input is an error, so the kernel works on |x|. It computes t = |x| as max(-x, x) with ACC.SUB.FIRST then ACC.MAX, stores it (exact, since the row has the same scale and grid as x) and reloads it. Then e = exp2(-t * log2e) and r = reciprocal(1 + e) = sigmoid(|x|), with the 1 broadcast by MULT.EE from a ones row resident in R0. Finally y = max(x * r, x * e * r): for x >= 0 the first term is silu, for x < 0 the second is. q = x * e is stored and reloaded so the negative branch is a product with no x - x*r cancellation. Each intermediate (t, e, r, q) is a round trip through XMEM via ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE (ISA idiom A8), quantized to the case's NX8 type, in two reused scratch rows. log2(e) is the sum of two exactly representable MULT constants (1.4375 + 0.00518798828125, relative error 4.9e-6), because one 8-bit NX8 constant is 0.4 % off. They are declared as single-choice float params with defaults, so a query needs only numel. Domain: numel a multiple of 128, from 128 to 1048320. The upper limit is NX8 XMEM, which addresses 16384 rows (x + y + 3 scratch). It covers 15 of the 24 signatures, and the 9 larger ones must be split on the host into calls of at most 1048320 elements (elementwise, so any split works). The tolerance is FP32_ORDER in fp32 (measured 9.5e-7) and 2 NX8 steps in NX8 (measured worst 2 steps on the negative branch, from the three intermediate roundings). The reference is the exact x * sigmoid(x) with the kernel's log2(e) constant; it does not model the intermediate roundings. All tested signatures run in the default tier up to numel 29568. 81920, 393216, 786432 and 1048320 are nightly (e4), and all pass.

host_steps: broadcast = true: expand b to a's shape before the call (the kernel adds same-shape tensors; the query does not say which axis b broadcasts along)
operands = scalar: write the scalar as b's first element (the kernel reads b[0] only)
name: add_exact
notes: One XMEM row (128 elements) per iteration, 2 words per row, all hardware instructions, in e4, e5, dynamic and fp32. The IPU has no vector add, so each addend passes through the multiplier against CR1 (1.0 as a MULT constant in every mode, an exact identity) and the accumulator sums them: word 1 is MULT.RC.VE a[r] x CR1 + ACC.ADD.FIRST, word 2 is MULT.VE b[r] x CR1 (tensor mode, b's row in R0) or MULT.EE R0[0] x CR1 (scalar mode, b[0] broadcast to all lanes) + ACC.ADD + ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE identity in the same word. The FP32 sum of two decoded elements is the reference's sum, so the only approximation is the NX8 store's rounding, which the harness applies to the golden too: every variant passes at EXACT. Loads run one word ahead of their MULT (MULT reads its registers at cycle start): word 1 loads b[r] into R0, word 2 loads a[r + 1] into R_CYCLIC, so the last iteration reads one row past a (the next region, never used). Scalar mode stores b[0] in the padding lanes of a partial last row, past numel. broadcast is declared (true and false) but ignored, because the query gives no broadcast shape: the host expands b first. b keeps numel elements in scalar mode too (tensor shapes cannot depend on a str parameter), of which only b[0] is read. Domain: numel 1 to 699008, the NX8 XMEM limit for three regions (5461 rows). It covers 20 of the 24 signatures; the 4 larger ones must be split on the host into calls of at most 699008 elements (elementwise, so any split works). Tested in the default tier: every covered signature size (1, 256, 257 scalar; 512, 768, 1024, 2048, 4096, 4112, 8224, 32768, 49152, 65536, 75264, 100352, 131072, 196608, 200704, 262144 tensor) plus odd sizes; 524288 and 699008 (e4, both modes) are nightly, and all pass.

operands = scalar: write the scalar as b's first element (the kernel reads b[0] only)
name: mul_exact
notes: One XMEM row (128 elements) per iteration, all hardware instructions, in e4, e5, dynamic and fp32. a, b and y are 1-D [numel] tensors, so any numel works: ceil(numel / 128) rows, zero past numel. Tensor mode (operands = "tensor") loads a row of a into R_CYCLIC and the same row of b into R0, multiplies them with MULT.RC.VV, and stores with ACC.ADD.FIRST + ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE identity in the same word: 2 words per row (two loads share the one LOAD slot). Scalar mode (operands = "scalar") loads b's first row into R0 once, and MULT.RC.VE with the LR source LR0 = 0 broadcasts R0[0]: 1 word per row. Each next row is loaded one word ahead (MULT reads its registers at cycle start), so the last iteration reads one row past a (and b), which is the next region and never used. The product of two decoded elements is exact in FP32, so the only approximation is the NX8 store's rounding, which the harness applies to the golden too: every variant passes at EXACT. broadcast is declared (true and false) but ignored, because the query gives no broadcast shape: the host expands b first. A kernel-side row broadcast would need that shape. Since tensor shapes cannot depend on a str parameter, b keeps numel elements in scalar mode too, of which only b[0] is read. Domain: numel 1 to 699008, the NX8 XMEM limit for three regions (5461 rows). It covers 18 of the 24 signatures, and the 6 larger ones must be split on the host into calls of at most 699008 elements (elementwise, so any split works; a scalar call repeats b[0] in each). Tested in the default tier: numel 1, 64, 128, 200, 256, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 8224, 16384, 32768, and 65536 and 262144 (e4 and fp32), across both modes. 524288 and 699008 (e4, both modes) are nightly, and all pass.

name: softmax_exp2_nx8_e4
notes: One softmax row at a time, in four passes over its ceil(n / 128) XMEM rows (chunks), all hardware instructions, in e4 and fp32. Pass 1: m = max x (AGG.MAX of x * 1 into R_ACC[0]), stored alone in a scratch row. Pass 2: num = exp2(c (x - m)) with c = log2(e) as two exactly representable MULT constants (1.4375 + 0.00518798828125, relative error 4.9e-6), computed hi x - hi m + lo x - lo m with m broadcast from R1[0], and stored into y, which is the numerator buffer. Pass 3: S = SUM num (AGG.SUM of the reloaded rows), r = reciprocal(S) stored alone. Pass 4: y = num * r, over the numerators. exp2 of a positive input is an emulator error, so m must be exactly max x: it is stored alone in its row (its own scale), where e4 holds it exactly, unlike a packed vector of 128 row maxima (one shared scale) as the FP32 softmax kernels keep; then every product is exact and x - m <= 0. The last chunk's DS (n - 128 (cpr - 1) valid elements) keeps its zero padding lanes out of exp2 (they would be positive when m < 0) and out of the sum. Cost: 14 words per row plus 7 per chunk. Domain: dim_last true, n 1..384, rows 1..2730; the box's corner, 2 * 2730 * 3 + 1 = 16381 rows, fits NX8 XMEM (16384). It covers 17 of the 24 signatures; five n = 256 calls with more than 2730 rows need a host row split, and n = 1500 is out of the domain. Tolerance: FP32_ORDER in fp32 (measured 1.9e-8), 2 NX8 steps in e4 (measured worst 2: the numerator and 1 / sum round to e4 before y). The reference is the exact softmax(x c ln 2) with the kernel's constant; it does not model the intermediate roundings. The default tier runs 48 tests (n = 1, 8, 32, 64, 99, 100, 128, 129, 256, 257, 384; negative-only, wide and constant logits; every n = 257 signature); the nightly tier runs n = 32 x 640, 64 x 512 / 768, 99 x 1188, 256 x 1024 / 2048 / 2304 and the corner 384 x 2730, all passing.

name: layernorm_rsqrt_nx8
notes: One token at a time, each ceil(channels / 128) XMEM rows (chunks), five passes over the chunks, all hardware instructions (rsqrt is ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE rsqrt), in e4 and fp32. P1: m' = SUM x (kh + kl), where kh + kl = 1 / channels are two fill rows (kh rounded to 4 bits by a closed-form expression over channels, kl the rest, rounded by the store). A: d = x - m' stored as d_hi + d_lo (the program reloads the stored e4 row, subtracts it from the accumulator it still holds and stores the rest: about 8 significant bits); m' is subtracted through a 1.0 / 0.0 lane-indicator row, so padding lanes stay 0. B: V = SUM d^2 and T = SUM d. Scalars (one element per row, so each has its own scale): delta = T / channels (one Newton step for the inexact 1 / channels), var = V / channels - delta^2 + eps clamped at 0, r = rsqrt(var) stored in unsigned e1 (8 significant bits, via a second QF half) and split into e4 r_hi + r_lo. C: n = (d - delta) r stored as n_hi + n_lo. D: y = n gamma + beta, stored once in e4. 23 words per chunk plus 47 per token (768 channels: 185 cycles per token; 2560 x 256: 129803 cycles). Without the Newton step a token of equal values came out as beta +- gamma; with it, y = beta to 0.002. Tolerance: fp32 FP32_ORDER; e4 is held to an absolute bound (rtol 0.125 = one e4 step of y, atol 2^-7), not NX8 steps: y = n gamma + beta cancels near 0, where the golden row's grid is far finer than the 8-bit intermediates (up to 70 steps there), so NX8_STEP cannot hold for any LayerNorm that stores intermediates in NX8. Measured against the exact LayerNorm (float64): worst excess over one e4 step is 0.0029 in the default tier and 0.0053 in the nightly tier (atol 0.004 failed 4 of the 13 nightly cases); the rest of the error is y's own e4 rounding. eps is a parameter with three NX8-exact choices (1.0014e-5, 9.98e-7, 0; default the first) because 1e-5 itself is not an NX8 MULT constant; it is added inside rsqrt as torch does. Domain: channels 1..2560, tokens 1..406, layout channels_last; the box corner 2560 x 406 uses 16346 of the 16384 NX8 rows. It covers 17 of the 24 signatures; the 7 with more than 406 tokens need a host split over tokens (rows are independent). The reference is the exact torch LayerNorm; the kernel's intermediate roundings are not modelled. The default tier runs 51 tests (channels 1, 8, 100, 128, 129, 200 and every signature channel count; mean 6 sigma from 0, outlier channels, constant tokens, the other eps values, 768 x 1/49/50/64/99); the nightly tier runs the real signature shapes up to 1152 x 256 and 2560 x 256 and the corner 2560 x 406, all 13 passing.
